what_was_built: canonical/runtime/repeat_execution_spectrum_v1.py -- Famas-style (arXiv 2509.13782) repeat-execution spectrum attribution, producing the `verified_coverage` boolean that universal_learning_contract_v1.route_input gates on

instrument_state.note: an earlier connection attempt succeeded at TCP but never answered; the cause was the missing --remote-allow-origins flag, not a dead browser. A socket that connects is not a socket that responds.

measurement.policy: click START, then pick one of three ordinal radio positions by seed, then Submit. Runs 0-2 deliberately omitted the selection and submit.
measurement.first_finding: raw Ochiai named `start`, which was present in all 12 runs including the one success. An action consistent with every outcome cannot explain the difference between them. Fixed with a discriminator guard (0 < runs_with < runs_total).
measurement.second_finding: after the guard, Ochiai named `submit` at 0.8040. But submit failed only in runs that had already chosen a wrong option (success rate 1/9), whereas select:1 and select:2 never succeeded (0/3) and select:0 did (1/3). Ochiai's frequency term rewards ubiquity and named the frequent innocent action. Co-occurrence with failure is not causation even across repeated runs.
measurement.resolution: outcome contrast (does ANY run containing this action succeed) is now computed alongside Ochiai. Certified attribution requires BOTH to name the same action.

what_this_proves: the GUI bench is live and a real MiniWob episode can be driven end to end by CDP
a MiniWob task CAN produce genuine outcome variance (1 success / 11 failures), which is the precondition Famas needs
spectrum attribution ALGORITHMS alone are insufficient here: two standard statistics disagree, and trusting either one alone would have manufactured a false cause
the module refuses rather than certifies, so no false verified_coverage entered the learning contract
what_this_does_NOT_prove: that repeat-execution attribution works on GUI tasks in general -- this is ONE task, ONE policy, 12 runs
that verified_coverage can be honestly True for a GUI step -- on this task it was False
any improvement in the 26/130 reach number, which this round did not re-measure
the_open_question_this_exposes: the spectum needs a policy that varies the SUSPECTED cause while holding everything else fixed. This policy varied the selection but added/removed the submit step at the same time, confounding the two. The next measurement must hold the action set constant across runs so only the candidate action varies.
